title: 20. See You Tomorrow
reviewMethod: English read-aloud translation compared with every original Korean page

pages.text: I'm the Rainbow Class teacher. Every morning, I wait by the sparkling clean classroom door. When it opens with a jingle, Hori, Kongi, and Dubu bounce inside. Good morning, Teacher! Oh, another lively day is beginning.

First, Hori looked ready to cry. Teacher, I left my backpack at home. His eyes filled with tears. I gave him a gentle hug. It's okay. These things happen. Today we'll share my crayons. At last, Hori smiled shyly.

While drawing, Kongi spilled the water cup. Splash! Water covered the desk. Kongi stamped those little feet, not knowing what to do. I hurried over with a cloth. It's okay. These things happen. We can wipe it up together.

Toto and Bori argued while playing with blocks. That's mine! No, I had it first! Toto was angry, and Bori was tearful. I sat gently between them and held their hands. Shall we talk one at a time? I'll listen to both of you.

Next came Dubu. While running happily, Dubu knocked down the tall block castle the friends had built. Crash! Dubu's ears drooped, and their head lowered. I patted Dubu's back. It's okay. These things happen. We can build an even better castle together.

When the fuss was over, laughter filled the Rainbow Class again. We sang together and enjoyed a delicious lunch. I quietly watched those little faces. Even after tumbles, spills, and arguments, we could laugh together again.
Before long, the sun began to set outside. Friends, it's time to go home. Let's get our backpacks. Hori and Kongi put on their coats and shoes. Outside, their moms were waiting and waving.

But the children lingered by the door. Their feet seemed unwilling to move. Teacher, I want to stay longer! Hori held my hand with both of his. Toto and Bori nodded with disappointed faces. Oh, do you love the Rainbow Class that much?

I knelt and hugged each child. You played so well today. Go home, sleep well, and rest, so tomorrow can be fun, too. At last, the children smiled. See you tomorrow, Teacher! Waving, they ran to their moms, one by one.

After all the children left, the Rainbow Class grew quiet. I smiled as I put away the scattered blocks and crayons. Today's tumbles and laughter had made another bright, precious day. Sleep well, Rainbow Class. See you tomorrow.
